top_stories.title: 18 insights from SailPoint’s Navigate event: Enterprises race to bring identity security for AI agents up to machine speed
top_stories.summary: SailPoint's Navigate event surfaced 18 key insights on the emerging challenge of securing AI agent identities at enterprise scale. Key findings include that AI agents now number in the thousands within organizations, are accumulating unintended access permissions, and are driving demand for machine-speed identity governance capabilities.

top_stories.title: Tenable Identity Exposure SaaS Has CVSS 9.9 Command Injection That Hands Attackers SYSTEM on the Domain Controller
top_stories.summary: A critical command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-106126) with a CVSS score of 9.9 has been discovered in Tenable Identity Exposure, a SaaS-based Active Directory security and identity threat detection platform. The flaw allows attackers to achieve SYSTEM-level access on the domain controller, representing a complete compromise of the identity infrastructure the product is designed to protect.

top_stories.title: How to keep AI agents within their permissions
top_stories.summary: The article addresses the challenge of AI agents operating beyond their assigned permissions using valid credentials, a gap in traditional access control models. Token Security outlines an approach for enforcing agent-specific authorization policies to constrain AI agent behavior within defined permission boundaries.

top_stories.title: The Third-Party Agent Problem: Why Security Built for AI You Chose Misses the Agents You Didn't
top_stories.summary: A new report, the 2026 State of Agent Security Report, finds that approximately 1,280 third-party products now embed AI agents, of which only 282 authenticate through SSO, leaving roughly 1,000 invisible to identity infrastructure. The findings highlight a governance gap where AI agents operating outside standard authentication flows cannot be managed or monitored by existing IAM tooling.

top_stories.title: The AI Velocity Paradox: Why Security Is Decades Behind AI Ambition
top_stories.summary: SailPoint's "Horizons of Identity Security" report identifies a "velocity paradox" where enterprises deploy autonomous AI agents while relying on legacy, human-speed identity security architectures. The report highlights the gap between AI-driven business operations and outdated security controls as a critical challenge for identity security programs.

news.title: Credential-Stealing GitHub Actions Workflows Planted in Tens of Thousands of Repositories
news.summary: A credential-stealing campaign has compromised two high-profile open-source maintainer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows into over 340 repositories. The attacker used the compromised account of pyxel author Takashi Kitao to push malicious workflows to 27 repositories, with the broader campaign targeting credential theft at scale across open-source projects.

news.title: PCI SSC calls for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data
news.summary: The PCI Security Standards Council has published advisory guidance on AI security in payment environments, covering governance, access controls, and defenses against AI-assisted attacks. The document includes recommendations on access controls for AI systems handling cardholder data, including human approval requirements for AI agent actions.

news.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
news.summary: Citrix has released patches for a critical memory overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-107406) in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that can lead to remote code execution or denial-of-service. The flaw is specifically triggered under SAML deployment configurations, making it directly relevant to organizations using these products for federated identity and authentication.

news.title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
news.summary: FBI and six allied nations reported that Integrity Technology Group, a Chinese cybersecurity company, conducted email theft against government, law enforcement, healthcare, and religious organizations in Southeast Asia. The hackers operated a portal allowing third-party access to stolen emails and used scanning tools to identify website vulnerabilities.

news.title: ‘The gap was not the awareness’: The company phishing trainings you loathe aren’t enough when nearly 1 in 4 security pros say their MFA is optional
news.summary: A survey found that nearly 1 in 4 security professionals report that MFA is optional at their organization, despite 44% acknowledging that an AI-driven phishing attack successfully breached their company last year. The findings highlight a gap between perceived security posture and actual MFA deployment practices among organizations.

news.title: U.S. Offers Up to $10 Million for Tips on Zhang Yu, Charged in HAFNIUM Hacks
news.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information on Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in connection with the 2021 HAFNIUM Microsoft Exchange Server attacks. The HAFNIUM attacks exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange Server, compromising tens of thousands of organizations' email systems and authentication infrastructure worldwide.

news.title: ID Dataweb Named "Overall ID Management Solution of the Year" in the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards Program
news.summary: ID Dataweb has been named "Overall ID Management Solution of the Year" in the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards Program. The award recognizes the company's identity threat detection and risk mitigation capabilities for enterprises.

news.title: Anugal Announces U.S. SAP IDM Readiness Campaign Ahead of 2027 Maintenance Deadline
news.summary: Anugal has launched a U.S. campaign to help enterprises prepare for the SAP Identity Management (SAP IDM) end-of-maintenance deadline in 2027. The campaign focuses on uncovering hidden SAP IDM dependencies, maintaining governance continuity, and reducing migration risk for organizations needing to transition away from SAP IDM.

news.title: The people who know passkeys best are still typing passwords
news.summary: A Yubico and Okta survey of 1,890 technology and security professionals across nine countries found that 43% still use username and password as their primary sign-in method for work accounts. This occurs despite 87% of respondents reporting familiarity with passkeys, highlighting a gap between passkey awareness and adoption among technical professionals.

news.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
news.summary: SonicWall has released hotfixes addressing four vulnerabilities in its SMA1000 secure remote access appliances, including a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF flaw. The critical flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to send requests through the appliance to reach internal network functions, affecting devices used to manage remote worker access to corporate networks and applications.

news.title: Browser-in-browser attacks use fake Meta Muse Ad lure to steal credentials
news.summary: A browser-in-browser (BitB) phishing attack is targeting users with fake Meta Muse ads to steal credentials. The attack creates convincing fake browser windows to trick users into entering login credentials on fraudulent authentication pages.

news.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude imitated in fake ads that steal credentials and MFA codes
news.summary: Cybercriminals are running fake advertisements impersonating AI tools ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to steal credentials and MFA codes from victims. The attacks specifically target advertiser accounts that have preloaded credit cards and funds, using credential theft and MFA bypass techniques.

news.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
news.summary: Kiteworks and Citrix faced separate zero-day vulnerability incidents requiring emergency response measures, with Kiteworks instructing customers to power down its platform during a nine-hour window. Citrix drew criticism for remaining silent about reported attacks before releasing a patch for its affected product.

news.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
news.summary: A vulnerability in SWIFT banking and government middleware has been identified that enables remote code execution (RCE). The flaw can be exploited to bypass hardware-based MFA in high-security environments, with patching recommended as the immediate mitigation.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official inquiry into the breach of the identity verification provider.
